gaps:
GAPS IN THE MARKET AND IN COMPETITOR OFFERINGS, version 2 (2026-11-04)
Synthesized from 577 caregiving reviews and posts about the 10 competitors in the table, plus 825 caregiver posts on Reddit. (Lively 58) means 58 Lively items say it. (Reddit 132) means 132 Reddit caregiver posts.

1. Nobody gets the rest of the family to actually help.
It's the biggest caregiver problem: doing it alone (Reddit 217), and siblings won't share the work (Reddit 63). Competitors share information, not work. CaringBridge is praised because one update reaches everyone (CaringBridge 49), but it isn't built for day-to-day coordination (CaringBridge 3). In group chats, requests get silence or a 'like' (Group texts 10), and being in the chat doesn't mean helping (Group texts 7). Only small signs of relatives taking on tasks exist: Lotsa sign-ups (Lotsa 3) and asking someone to cover a shift (Group texts 3).

2. Relatives can't get their own way into the parent's accounts.
Reddit shows banks and agencies refusing the caregiver (Reddit 46), lost passwords (Reddit 32) and codes going to the parent's phone (Reddit 22). MyChart works once a caregiver is in (MyChart 13), but there's no caregiver login, so families share the parent's password (MyChart 7), and proxy access is hard to get (MyChart 8). Linking family is confusing on Lively (Lively 13), and sharing breaks between caregivers on Medisafe (Medisafe 4). Everplans needs the parent to set everything up ahead of time, and no caregiver use was found. No competitor covers banks or insurers.

3. Safety tools work for the older person but fail the family.
The button reaches help (Lively 15, Medical Guardian 5), but the family app fails. Location is wrong or stale (Lively 58), sign-in fails or the app crashes (Lively 37, Medical Guardian 16), and alerts to family come late or never (Lively 27), or family isn't told (Medical Guardian 6). Parents stop wearing the device (Medical Guardian 5) or find it hard to use (Lively 13). Families on Reddit want the alert to reach them, not only a dispatcher (Reddit 59 safety posts).

4. Information gets lost between people, especially medication changes.
In group chats, details get buried, causing missed appointments and near double doses (Group texts 10). Paper stays with one person, so family miss changes (Paper notebook 6). In Medisafe the caregiver's view goes out of sync (Medisafe 3), and you can't tell whose dose it is (Medisafe 2). On Reddit, medication changes not being shared caused double doses or mix-ups (Reddit 24).

5. Papers, records and power of attorney have no real home.
On Reddit: POA missing, rejected or delayed (Reddit 29), and papers scattered or lost (Reddit 22). Paper records pile up and can't be found when a doctor asks (Paper notebook 7). MyChart records are hard to share outside the app (MyChart 3), so siblings get screenshots (MyChart 3). Caring Village stores documents (Caring Village 3), but old records can't be kept or found (Caring Village 2). No competitor helps with POA.

6. No one covers the whole job, so families stitch tools together.
Each row covers one piece: updates, records, medications or safety. Paper is used alongside digital calendars, chats and photos (Paper notebook 11). Group chats run next to shared calendars and docs (Group texts 6). CaringBridge families add group texts and spreadsheets for the daily work (CaringBridge 3).

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: whether people would pay for any of this. Companies outside these 10. Reviews lean toward strong opinions, and Reddit venting over-represents conflict. Everplans (1 caregiving review) and Lotsa (4 items) are too thin to judge.

FOR THE OWNER TO DECIDE: which of these gaps to be better at than the competitors, and why.
uvo_title: SUMMARIZE THE UNIQUE VALUE OPPORTUNITIES, version 2 (2026-11-04). Open problems, nothing chosen.
grid: Area
What competitors do well
What competitors do not do well
What our business could do differently (open problem, not a feature)
How strong is the evidence?
1. Getting the family to share the work
Telling everyone at once saves the caregiver time (CaringBridge 49, CaringBridge 19). Keeping the family on the same page (Caring Village 10). Signing up helpers for tasks (Lotsa 3).

They share news, not work. CaringBridge isn't built for daily coordination (CaringBridge 3). Getting everyone to join is hard (Caring Village 2). Requests get silence (Group texts 10), and being in the chat doesn't mean helping (Group texts 7).
Help the main caregiver get relatives to take on and follow through on real tasks, not just read updates.
Strong need: the biggest Reddit theme (Reddit 217). Competitor evidence is thin on tasks.
2. Relatives' own access to the parent's accounts
Once in, a caregiver can see results, message doctors and manage several people (MyChart 13, MyChart 12, MyChart 11). Medisafe lets a relative watch doses (Medisafe 4).

No caregiver login, so families share passwords (MyChart 7). Proxy setup is hard (MyChart 8). Linking is confusing (Lively 13). Sharing breaks between caregivers (Medisafe 4). Banks and insurers aren't covered by anyone (Reddit 46).
Help a relative get and keep their own access to what the parent needs managed, without sharing the parent's login.
Strong: second-largest Reddit theme (Reddit 132), and seen in competitor reviews too.
3. Safety alerts that reach the family
Reassurance (Lively 25), seeing where the person is (Lively 23), and quick help from an operator (Lively 15, Medical Guardian 5).
Wrong location (Lively 58), late or missing alerts to family (Lively 27), sign-in failures (Lively 37, Medical Guardian 16), and parents not wearing it (Medical Guardian 5).
Help the family trust that they'll know quickly and correctly when something happens.
Strong complaints, but a crowded market with device costs. Reddit need is smaller (Reddit 59).
4. Passing on medication changes between caregivers
Keeping one loved one's complicated schedule on track (Medisafe 10), managing several people's meds (Medisafe 5), and paper checklists for in-home helpers (Paper notebook 4).
Changes get buried or stay with one person (Group texts 10, Paper notebook 6). Caregiver views go out of sync (Medisafe 3). You can't tell whose dose it is (Medisafe 2).
Help every caregiver see the same, current medication information, so no dose is missed or doubled.
Medium: a real risk (Reddit 24), but medication apps are crowded.
5. Papers, records and power of attorney
MyChart records are ready to hand to others (MyChart 5). Caring Village stores documents (Caring Village 3). A binder lets a stand-in caregiver step in (Paper notebook 3).
Paper can't be searched (Paper notebook 7). Old records get lost (Caring Village 2). Sharing outside MyChart is hard (MyChart 3). No one helps when a POA is rejected (Reddit 29).
Help the family keep the parent's key papers and records findable and usable when a bank or doctor asks.
Medium to strong need (Reddit 97). No competitor addresses POA.
6. Money and who pays
Easy to start: CaringBridge and Lotsa are free, Caring Village has a free plan, and some find Lively good value (Lively 6).

Paying for a service that doesn't work, with no refunds (Lively 11). Extra fees and hard refunds (Medical Guardian 5). Donation prompts feel pushy (CaringBridge 2). Caring Village's free plan stops at 2 members.
Find out who would pay for family coordination, and how much. Unknown today.
Weak: no evidence on willingness to pay for coordination.
7. Health data and consent
Families trust invite-only spaces (CaringBridge 6). Caring Village and CaringBridge say they don't sell health data.

'Friends' can see private medical details (Caring Village 2). The parent's privacy wishes clash with family access (MyChart 6). Security steps block caregivers (MyChart 3). Private things end up in the wrong chat (Group texts 2). Medisafe may share data with drug makers.
Let family help while respecting what the parent wants shared.
Medium: more a design risk to plan around than a reason people choose a tool.
